# ui

Namespace-scope declarations of `ui` from the themes headers.

## Enumerations

### ButtonState

```cpp
enum class ButtonState
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

The interaction state a control derives from its input flags. Focus is not one of them. The focus visual is a separate ring a control draws on top of whichever of these four states it is in, so a focused and hovered control keeps its hover look.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Normal` | At rest. |
| `Hover` | The pointer is over the control. |
| `Pressed` | Held down by the pointer or the keyboard. |
| `Disabled` | The control is disabled; wins over the other three. |

### CornerPreference

```cpp
enum class CornerPreference
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

How the corners of the system-drawn window frame are rounded. An era theme sets this so the frame matches the content, so a Windows 95 theme asks for square corners. Windows 11 only.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Default` | The system decides: round on Windows 11. |
| `DoNotRound` | Square corners. |
| `Round` | The standard window radius. |
| `RoundSmall` | The smaller menu and flyout radius. |

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

How a control marks that something opens, drops down or expands: [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander), [TreeView](../controls/tree-view.md#uitreeview), [NavigationShell](../controls/navigation-shell.md#uinavigationshell), [Breadcrumb](../controls/breadcrumb.md#uibreadcrumb), [DropdownButton](../controls/dropdown-button.md#uidropdownbutton), [SplitButton](../controls/split-button.md#uisplitbutton), [NumberBox](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox)'s spin buttons and a menu's submenu arrow. ### ThemePopupShadow

```cpp
enum class ThemePopupShadow
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

Which drop shadow an open popup casts (render/OverlayShadow.hpp). Fluent's two-light shadow follows from an elevation scale, where every kind of surface has a height. Aero casts no shadow under a button, card or panel. Its only shadow is an offset block with a 5 px fall-off under a menu, tooltip or drop-down. Defaults to the Fluent shadow.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `FluentTwoLight` | Fluent's soft two-light elevation shadow. |
| `AeroDropShadow` | An offset block with a 5 px fall-off, as Luna and Aero draw it. |
| `None` | No shadow at all. Menus, drop-downs and dialogs are plain rectangles on the surface below them. |

### ThemePopupAnimation

```cpp
enum class ThemePopupAnimation
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

How a menu ([MenuFlyout](../controls/menu-flyout.md#uimenuflyout), the menu bar's menus, a context menu) and a drop-down list ([ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox)) come into view. Every era animates these differently:
- Fluent 2, Fluent, MDL2 and Metro (the defaults): a menu slides out from its own edge over 250 ms and fades out over 83 ms. A drop-down list appears at once.
- Aero and Luna follow the system's animation settings. A menu fades in when menu fading is on, slides in when it is off, and does neither when menu animation is off. A drop-down list slides open when list box animation is on. Both run 200 ms, and a menu closes at once. [resolve_theme()](#resolve_theme) reads the settings from [OsThemeSnapshot](os-theme-snapshot.md).
- Windows 9x, 3.x and 1.x/2.x: no animation.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Slide` | Slides out from its own edge. |
| `Fade` | Fades in. |
| `None` | Appears at once. |

### ThemeVariant

```cpp
enum class ThemeVariant
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

The design language (era) the whole UI is drawn in, chosen independently of the Windows version the app runs on. ThemeVariant::System, the default, draws the look of the running Windows: Fluent 2 on Windows 11 and Fluent before it. Fluent2 is the primary target.

`System`, `Fluent2` and `Fluent` are always available. The era themes (`Mdl2` to `Windows1x`) are linked into an app only once it calls [enable_era_themes()](#enable_era_themes). Before that, asking for one draws the System look.

Dark and light are not variants. They are set by [ThemeMode](#thememode), which by default follows the system. `Fluent2`, `Fluent`, `Metro` and `Mdl2` have a dark and a light palette and honor [ThemeMode](#thememode) and [ThemeRequest::accent_override](theme-request.md). Every other variant has one fixed, light palette and ignores both ([theme_variant_supports_dark_mode()](#theme_variant_supports_dark_mode)).

Under high contrast every variant draws its own era's high-contrast look. Windows 9x, 3.x and 1.x take the contrast colors as one more color scheme, Luna and Aero fall back to the Classic look as XP and 7 did, and Metro, MDL2 and Fluent keep their shapes in contrast colors. The colors are the system's contrast theme while one is on, and the era's own contrast scheme when an app forces ThemeMode::HighContrast without one.

Example: 
```cpp
int run_retro()
{
    ui::Window retro{{
        .title = "Retro",
        .theme = ui::ThemeRequest{.variant = ui::ThemeVariant::Windows9x}, // light-only, ignores ThemeMode
    }};
    return ui::run(retro);
}
```

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `System` | The look of the running Windows: Fluent2 on Windows 11 and Fluent on Windows 10 and earlier ([OsThemeSnapshot::system_variant](os-theme-snapshot.md)). The default. A resolved [Theme](theme.md) never reports it. Its [Theme::variant](theme.md#variant) is the variant System stood for. |
| `Fluent2` | Fluent 2, Windows 11's design, whatever Windows the app runs on. The primary target, with resolve_high_contrast() under high contrast. |
| `Fluent` | Fluent 1: the original Fluent Design System as it shipped on Windows 10, from 1709 (2017) through early 2021. Follows dark and light mode and the accent, like Fluent2. Windows 11 is Fluent2. See resolve_fluent1() for what this variant changes. |
| `Mdl2` | MDL2 ("Microsoft Design Language 2"): Windows 10's original flat, square look with the accent as its only color, as it shipped from 1507 (2015-07-29) through 1703 (2017-04-11), before Fluent. No material, no elevation, and no rounded corners except the [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider) thumb and the [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch) track. Follows dark and light mode and the accent, like Fluent2, Fluent and Metro. Its colors come from the 24 base colors of an [Mdl2Palette](mdl2-palette.md), in a light and a dark set. The name is a press convention. No Microsoft document of the era uses it. |
| `Metro` | MDL ("Metro Design Language"): Windows 8 and 8.1 merged into one entry. It follows Windows 8.1, with its dark mode and user accent. |
| `Aero` | Aero: Windows Vista and 7 merged into one entry, defaulting to Windows 7's column. The two releases barely differ. The only change a control shows is disabled text, which went from `#808080` to `#6D6D6D`. Aero has no control accent, since the user's glass color tinted the frame, taskbar and Start menu but never a control. This variant ignores both [ThemeMode](#thememode)'s light and dark and [ThemeRequest::accent_override](theme-request.md). |
| `Luna` | Luna: Windows XP's default visual style. |
| `Windows9x` | Windows 9x: Windows 95, 98, and 2000 merged into one entry. Defaults to the Windows 95 and 98 "Windows Standard" scheme ([`ClassicPalette::windows_standard()`](classic-palette.md#windows_standard)). [ThemeRequest::classic_scheme](theme-request.md) swaps in any other [ClassicPalette](classic-palette.md), such as [`ClassicPalette::windows_standard_2000()`](classic-palette.md#windows_standard_2000). |
| `Windows3x` | Windows 3.x: before hot tracking, Active Desktop and the four-color bevel of Windows 95. |
| `Windows1x` | Early Windows: Windows 1.01 (1985-11) through 2.11 (1989-03), the design language Windows 3.0 replaced in May 1990. It has no sense of depth at all: no bevel, no gray `#C0C0C0` face, no light source, no highlight and shadow pair and no drop shadow. All of its chrome is black and white, and the only depth cue is a one-pixel frame line. It has ten colors, thirteen from 2.0, with no button face, selection or disabled-text color among them. That is why its colors are an [`EarlyPalette`](early-palette.md) instead of a [`ClassicPalette`](classic-palette.md), and its theme comes from [`Theme::early()`](theme.md#early) instead of [`Theme::classic()`](theme.md#classic). What sets "Windows 1" apart from "Windows 2" happens at 2.03 in December 1987, when windows stopped being tiled. This one variant covers both and defaults to the Windows 2.03 color palette. [`EarlyPalette::windows_1x_mono()`](early-palette.md#windows_1x_mono) and the other two palettes are one [ThemeRequest::early_scheme](theme-request.md) away. The four palettes are separate looks, so pick a version first, then a display type, and do not mix them. |

### ThemeMode

```cpp
enum class ThemeMode
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Which light, dark or contrast appearance a [ThemeRequest](theme-request.md) asks for.

Only the variants for which [theme_variant_supports_dark_mode()](#theme_variant_supports_dark_mode) is true tell Light and Dark apart. HighContrast applies to every variant.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `System` | Follow the system's light or dark setting as it changes (the default). |
| `Light` | Always light, whatever the system setting. |
| `Dark` | Always dark, whatever the system setting. |
| `HighContrast` | The system's contrast theme while one is on, otherwise the variant's own contrast colors (see [resolve_theme()](#resolve_theme)). |

### AnimationPreference

```cpp
enum class AnimationPreference
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Whether controls animate: follow the system's "Animation effects" setting, or force it either way.

With animations off, every transition the framework plays itself lands on its end state at once: control state tweens, transitions, implicit and brush transitions, popup motion, animated icons, animated scrolling and connected animations. Timers that are not animations (tooltip delay, caret blink, key repeat) keep running, and an indeterminate [ProgressBar](../controls/progress-bar.md#uiprogressbar) or [ProgressRing](../controls/progress-ring.md#uiprogressring) keeps moving, since that motion is what tells the user work is going on.

Example: 
```cpp
// A "Reduce motion" switch in an app's settings page:
void set_reduce_motion(bool reduce_motion)
{
    ui::ThemeRequest request = window.theme_request();
    request.animations       = reduce_motion ? ui::AnimationPreference::Off : ui::AnimationPreference::System;
    window.set_theme(request);
}
```

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `System` | Follow [OsThemeSnapshot::animations_enabled](os-theme-snapshot.md) as it changes (the default). |
| `On` | Always animate, whatever the system setting. |
| `Off` | Never animate, whatever the system setting. |

## Functions

### classic_lighter

```cpp
Color classic_lighter(const Color& c, float percent = 1.0f)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ClassicPalette.hpp`.

Lightens `c` the way the classic 3-D ramp is derived from a face color. The color's luminosity moves toward white by up to half the remaining distance, and `percent`, clamped to [0,1], scales that move. Hue, saturation and alpha are kept.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Color face  = ui::Color::from_rgba(128, 64, 128); // a custom face
const ui::Color light = ui::classic_lighter(face, 0.5f);    // the bevel's outer light ring
const ui::Color dark  = ui::classic_darker(face, 1.0f);     // the bevel's outer dark ring
```

### classic_darker

```cpp
Color classic_darker(const Color& c, float percent = 1.0f)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ClassicPalette.hpp`.

Darkens `c` the same way [classic_lighter()](#classic_lighter) lightens it. The luminosity moves toward black by up to a third, scaled by `percent`, which is clamped to [0,1]. Hue, saturation and alpha are kept.

### classic_bevel_ramp_from_face

```cpp
ClassicBevelRamp classic_bevel_ramp_from_face(const Color& face)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ClassicPalette.hpp`.

Derives the whole classic 3-D ramp from one face color. `light` is [`classic_lighter(face, 0.5)`](#classic_lighter), `highlight` is [`classic_lighter(face, 1.0)`](#classic_lighter), `shadow` is [`classic_darker(face, 0.5)`](#classic_darker) and `dark_shadow` is [`classic_darker(face, 1.0)`](#classic_darker).

When `face` is exactly one of the two standard grays, the ramp that era ships is returned as is, because neither can be derived:
- `0xC0C0C0` (Windows 95 and 98 SE): `0xDFDFDF`, white, `0x808080` and black. Its light ring sits between the face and the highlight.
- `0xD4D0C8` (Windows 2000, and XP's Classic scheme): the face itself, white, `0x808080` and `0x404040`. The light ring equals the face, and the dark ring is softer than black.

Any other face color, as in a custom scheme, gets the computed ramp.

Example: 
```cpp
// In a custom control's render_override(): a raised teal panel. Teal is no canonical gray, so its
// ramp is computed, with `highlight` equal to classic_lighter(face, 1.0f).
class TealPanelControl : public ui::Element
{
protected:
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext&) const override
    {
        const ui::Color            face = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 128, 128);
        const ui::ClassicBevelRamp ramp = ui::classic_bevel_ramp_from_face(face);
        renderer.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 0.0f, face);
        ui::draw_bevel_border(renderer, bounds(), ui::BorderStyle::Raised, ramp.light, ramp.highlight,
                              ramp.shadow, ramp.dark_shadow, 1.0f);
    }
};

// Windows 2000's gray gets its published ramp instead: `#D4D0C8` (the face itself), white,
// `#808080` and `#404040`.
const ui::ClassicBevelRamp win2000 = ui::classic_bevel_ramp_from_face(ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFD4D0C8));
```

### early_reverse_video

```cpp
std::pair<Color, Color> early_reverse_video(const Color& background, const Color& foreground)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/EarlyPalette.hpp`.

Reverse video, the era's only way to show a selected state, which is why the palettes above have no selection color. A selected run swaps its foreground and background. Returns the swapped pair as `{background, foreground}`.

The swap keeps the palette's own colors. Inverting each pixel instead would turn the 2.03 color palette's cyan menu red. On monochrome palettes both give the same result.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::EarlyPalette p         = ui::EarlyPalette::windows_2x_color();
const ui::Rect         item_rect = {0, 0, 80, 20};
const auto [fill, text] = ui::early_reverse_video(p.menu, p.menu_text); // a selected menu item
renderer.fill_rounded_rect(item_rect, 0.0f, fill);
renderer.draw_text("Open...", item_rect, text, theme.text_style);
```

### early_dither_gray

```cpp
Color early_dither_gray(const Color& ink, const Color& paper)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/EarlyPalette.hpp`.

The era's gray as one flat color. The era has no disabled-text color and grays disabled items with a 50 % checkerboard of ink and paper. [`Renderer`](../rendering/renderer.md) has no pattern fill, so this returns the checkerboard's average, the midpoint of the two colors. Black on white gives `#808080`, the gray the Windows 1.01 monochrome palette uses for the desktop and inactive captions.

Only the text grays out. A disabled push button keeps its frame, corners and border and grays its label.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::EarlyPalette p          = ui::EarlyPalette::windows_1x_mono();
const ui::Color        gray       = ui::early_dither_gray(p.window_text, p.window); // ~`#808080`
const ui::Rect         label_rect = {0, 0, 80, 20};
const bool             enabled    = false;
renderer.draw_text("Cancel", label_rect, enabled ? p.window_text : gray, theme.text_style);
```

### resolve_theme

```cpp
Theme resolve_theme(const ThemeRequest& request, const OsThemeSnapshot& os)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Resolves an app's request against the system's settings into a [Theme](theme.md). High contrast, when it is on because the system reports it or the app asked for ThemeMode::HighContrast, wins over every other color input (`mode`, `accent_override`, `classic_scheme`, `early_scheme`), since apps don't keep their brand colors under high contrast. `variant` still picks the era the contrast colors are drawn in. The system's contrast theme (`os.hc`) is the user's choice and always supplies the colors. A forced high contrast with no contrast theme on takes the variant's own contrast colors: Aquatic for Fluent 2, Windows 10's High Contrast Black for Fluent, MDL2 and Metro, the XP and Windows 98 High Contrast Black schemes for Luna, Aero and Windows 9x, Windows 3.1's Monochrome scheme, and the matching monochrome palette for Early Windows.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::OsThemeSnapshot os;
os.dark = true;

// The app asks for light, so the system being dark doesn't change the result.
const ui::Theme theme = ui::resolve_theme(ui::ThemeRequest{.mode = ui::ThemeMode::Light}, os);
window.pin_theme(theme);
```

### enable_era_themes

```cpp
void enable_era_themes()
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Links the era themes into the app, ThemeVariant::Mdl2 to ThemeVariant::Windows1x, with their window frames. Until it is called they are left out of the executable, and a [ThemeRequest](theme-request.md) asking for one draws ThemeVariant::System instead. Call it once, before the first window. Calling it again does nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
int main()
{
    ui::enable_era_themes();
    ui::Window window{{.title = "Retro", .theme = ui::ThemeRequest{.variant = ui::ThemeVariant::Luna}}};
    return ui::run(window);
}
```

### era_themes_enabled

```cpp
bool era_themes_enabled()
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Whether [enable_era_themes()](#enable_era_themes) was called, so the era variants draw as themselves.

### theme_variant_supports_dark_mode

```cpp
bool theme_variant_supports_dark_mode(ThemeVariant variant)
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

Whether `variant` tells [ThemeRequest::mode](theme-request.md)'s Dark and Light apart: true for System, Fluent2, Fluent, Metro and Mdl2. Every other variant has one fixed, light palette and looks the same whatever `mode` says, except ThemeMode::HighContrast, which still replaces its colors. A UI with a variant picker and a dark/light switch uses it to disable the switch when it would have no effect.

### os_theme

```cpp
OsThemeSnapshot os_theme()
```

Header: `winui/ui/themes/ThemeSource.hpp`.

What the operating system's theme is right now: light or dark, the accent color, high contrast. A window that follows the system already tracks this by itself; ask for it to pre-select a theme picker to match, or to resolve a theme before a window exists. A platform with no backend returns the defaults.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> dark{ui::os_theme().dark};
```
